resources.string: The fix is applied on boot, on audio connection, and every 30 minutes.

1. Connect your phone to your PC via USB.
2. Enable USB Debugging in your phone's Developer Options.
3. Open a terminal (CMD, PowerShell, or Bash) on your computer.
4. Copy, paste, and run the command below:

What this does:\nThis grants the app permission to modify hidden system flags (WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS) that are normally restricted. It allows the app to talk directly to the Android System Server to override safety thresholds and whitelists it from battery optimization so it can monitor connections reliably.
adb shell pm grant com.safe.comsafevolumefixer android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS; adb shell dumpsys deviceidle whitelist +com.safe.comsafevolumefixer

Safe Volume Fixer automates the process of bypassing Android's mandatory high-volume warnings. It works by monitoring system events and instantly resetting specific system flags:

• Auto-Bypass: It sets the system volume state to 'Acknowledged', so the warning popup never appears.

• CSD & History Wipe: It resets the legacy 20-hour timer and the newer Android 14+ "Calculated Sound Dose" (CSD) tracking. Crucially, it also wipes the hidden "Dose Records" history so the system never thinks you've exceeded your weekly limit.

• Continuous Protection: The fix is applied on device startup (even before unlock), every time headphones/Bluetooth are connected, and every 30 minutes via a background timer.

• Low Footprint: Runs as a lightweight background service with minimal battery impact.
